finding.message: src/presentation/invoice.controller.ts (presentation) skips layers to import src/persistence/invoice.repository.ts (persistence)

answer.explanation: InvoiceController sits in the presentation layer. At line 2 it imports InvoiceRepository from the persistence layer and injects it through the constructor (line 7). Its cancel() method (lines 14-16) then calls repo.markCancelled directly, so the business layer is skipped. The controller's other operation, issue() (lines 10-12), goes through InvoiceService in the business layer as expected. FF-S03 flags this because presentation should only reach persistence through the business layer. As written, cancelling an invoice bypasses any business rules for that state change, such as checking whether the invoice can be cancelled, auditing it or emitting domain events. It also ties the controller to how data is stored. The graph confirms the skip: there is a CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS edge and a CALLS edge from InvoiceController to InvoiceRepository, alongside the expected edges to InvoiceService. I was given no project docs, ADRs or comments on layering, so I found no declared intent and no declared exception for this dependency.

InvoiceController sits in the presentation layer. It imports InvoiceRepository from the persistence layer (line 2), receives it through its constructor (line 7), and its cancel() method calls repo.markCancelled(invoiceId) directly (line 15). The issue() path goes through the business layer (InvoiceService.issue, line 11), but the cancel path skips that layer and changes persisted invoice state with no business-layer logic in between. FF-S03 flags this because presentation should depend only on the layer directly below it (business), not jump to persistence. Here the jump means any cancellation rules (allowed state changes, authorization, side effects) can be bypassed, and the controller is tied to how storage works. No documentation, ADR or comment was provided that addresses this dependency. The fix is small and local: add a cancel operation to InvoiceService that wraps the repository call, then drop the repository import and injection from the controller. It ranks medium within the blocking tier because it is an unmediated write path, even though only one method is affected.
